context: Project ATLAS needs a clean, project-isolated canonical governance layer while reusing the pinned gbrain runtime for retrieval, MCP, and graph projection without coupling ATLAS policy to upstream internals.
hard_constraints: Confluence remains canonical fachliche Source of Truth.
Project scope is deterministic and never inferred from titles or model semantics.
Canonical data uses project_id, PostgreSQL RLS, separate service roles, proposals, approval evidence, and audit.
Core operation does not require paid model API credits.
Legacy embeddings, facts, links, and timelines are not migrated as canonical data.
Upstream source versions and licenses are pinned.
Productive agent publish remains blocked until all release gates pass.

candidates.name: Direct gbrain fork as canonical store
candidates.summary: Modify gbrain until its schema and permission model become the complete ATLAS canonical platform.

hard_constraint_results.notes: Pinned source has source_id scoping but not the full ATLAS canonical project_id/composite-FK contract.
Unmodified scopes do not implement the required proposal/approve/publish separation.
A deep fork would materially increase upstream merge cost.

non_risks: gbrain already provides useful retrieval and graph primitives
tradeoff_points: Less duplication versus much stronger coupling

candidates.name: ATLAS canonical core plus pinned gbrain projection
candidates.summary: Own registry, proposals, evidence, audit, and isolation in ATLAS; project approved revisions into gbrain for retrieval and graph capabilities.

hard_constraint_results.notes: The canonical core can implement project_id and composite keys independently of gbrain.
Proposal, approval, and publisher roles are ATLAS-owned.
Pinned adapter boundary limits upstream coupling.
VPS capacity and projection behavior require audit and pilot proof.

non_risks: Does not require a separate graph database
Does not require paid embedding APIs
tradeoff_points: More explicit components in exchange for lower upstream coupling

candidates.name: Separate full stack per project
candidates.summary: Run independent canonical and gbrain service/database sets for ATLAS, EasyTree, and Plumbline.

hard_constraint_results.notes: Process and database boundaries provide strong separation.
Resource and operational cost may be excessive on the target VPS.

non_risks: Cross-project database joins are structurally absent

strongest_counterargument: The overlay duplicates data and creates projection drift. A clean upstream-compatible gbrain extension could be simpler if it can natively satisfy project_id, RLS, proposal, approval, and publish separation with lower total upgrade cost.
decision_rationale: It satisfies the canonical governance requirements without a deep gbrain fork.
It preserves gbrain as a replaceable and rebuildable derived capability.
It supports the clean-rebuild and evidence policies.
It defers optional UI and Obsidian plugin choices rather than locking them into the backend.
rejected_alternatives: CAND-001 violates current canonical policy requirements without a deep fork.
CAND-003 is operationally disproportionate for three projects on one unaudited VPS.
consequences: A projector and checkpoint/reconciliation process are required.
gbrain write operations must be wrapped and project-scoped.
Canonical data definitions remain an ATLAS responsibility.
The graph UI can evolve independently from storage.

risks.statement: Canonical and gbrain projection state can drift.
risks.mitigation: Revision hashes, idempotent projection, checkpoints, reconciliation, and rebuild tests.

risks.statement: The target VPS may not sustain BGE-M3 and the full Compose topology.
risks.mitigation: ATLAS-16 audit and benchmark before runtime implementation.

risks.statement: Existing prototype history may be overwritten during repository migration.
risks.mitigation: No remote apply; require an explicit repository migration decision and PR-based change.

assumptions.statement: gbrain remains maintainable behind a narrow pinned adapter.
assumptions.review_trigger: First upstream upgrade or adapter contract break.

assumptions.statement: Projection latency acceptable for daily knowledge work can be achieved on the target VPS.

review_triggers: gbrain upstream provides native project_id/RLS/proposal semantics
Projection reconciliation fails a release gate
VPS audit shows the topology is not viable
A fourth production project materially changes isolation or capacity needs
Graph UI or Obsidian feedback requires canonical write semantics
